thread:
Ana: morning team — I'm primary until 16:00 UTC. Noticed p99 creeping up on the model-serving path, wanted to call this out before the shift gets busy. I'll list quick remedials below.

Devon: noted. I'm on secondary until 20:00. If we get a page, first try the KV cache warm-restart flow. Link in the checklist.

incident-bot: Pager triggered — ALERT: model-serving.latency.p99 > 2.5s (region: us-west). Pager id: pager/8765. Severity: S2.

Ana: acknowledging pager. Action plan (quick): 1) check autoscaler health (console.prod -> services/model-serving) 2) check GPU util + queue depth 3) inspect kv-cache eviction metrics -> if thrash, perform rolling restart of kv-cache pods 4) enable fallback routing to small-lr model if queue > 100.

Mike: copy. If you restart cache, prefer rolling with `--grace 30`. Script we use: `./scripts/cache-rotate.sh --grace 30` (in repo infra/ops). Avoid full cluster restart.

Lee: adding quick commands for reference:
```
# list cache pods
kubectl get pods -l app=kv-cache -n prod
# drain & delete one node (rolling)
kubectl cordon <pod-name>
kubectl delete pod <pod-name> -n prod
# watch rejoin
kubectl get pods -l app=kv-cache -w -n prod
```

Sam: FYI customer-impact: workspace `corp-alpha` has ~40 queued requests and a few timeouts; currently low-blast radius but watch for escalation. Ticket created: #12345.

Ana: toggling fallback route now (small-lr). Config UI: https://console.redwood.com/configs/fallback-routing — this should reduce p99 while we remediate cache.

Devon: oncall checklist reminder: 1) confirm prim/sec owners 2) follow runbook steps (cache restart, autoscaler check) 3) post status to #incidents 4) update ticket + customer note 5) escalate to oncall-exec if unresolved >30m.

oncall-bot: Reminder to fill shift-note template when swapping primary: https://docs.redwood.com/templates/shift-notes — include mitigations and ticket links.

Mike: quick rollback option if this is a bad deploy: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --service model-serving --to-tag v2026-03-12` — only if metrics point to deploy regressions.

Ana: starting KV-cache rolling restart now. I'll restart one pod at a time and monitor p99. Posting updates every 5m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

incident-bot: Update: auto-fallback engaged (small-lr) at +3m, some reduction in p99 observed.

Ana: after two pods restarted, nodes are rejoining and evictions dropped. p99 trending down toward 1.2s. Leaving runbook pointers in ticket.

Devon: looks stable for now. Request: raise autoscaler p99 threshhold to reduce noise — current setting urgent. I'll file a follow-up perf ticket.

Sam: customer comms drafted and sent to support lead; nothing required from legal. Ticket #12345 updated with mitigations and timeline.

Ana: closing loop — KV rolling restart completed, fallback routing active, p99 stable. Root-cause suspected: transient KV eviction storm during background model retrain. Runbook refs added to ticket:
- KV cache warm restart: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/kv-cache-warm-restart
- Fallback routing guide: https://console.redwood.com/configs/fallback-routing
- Autoscaler quick checks: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/autoscaler-triage

Devon: please annotate any config changes you made in the runbook so next oncall can follow.

Ana: handing primary to Mike at 16:00 UTC. Shift note: `shift:primary->Mike | mitigations applied | ticket #12345`. Leaving brief runbook checklist in notes. :white_check_mark:

Mike: taking primary, got the links. Thanks for the quick mitigation. I'll keep an eye on p50/p95 for the next hour.

Ana: thanks team — will follow up on perf tickets and add a small regression test to catch eviction storms.
